content: 1. Remicade, Inflectra, Renflexis, Ixifi, and Avsola are indicated for reducing signs and symptoms, inhibiting the progression of structural damage, and improving physical function in patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis when used in combination with methotrexate. The recommended dose is 3 mg/kg administered intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 8 weeks. If an incomplete response is observed, the dose may be increased to 10 mg/kg or the dosing frequency adjusted to every 4 weeks. 2. These medications are also indicated for reducing signs and symptoms of active psoriatic arthritis, inhibiting structural damage progression, and improving physical function. The recommended dose is 5 mg/kg intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 8 weeks. They may be used with or without methotrexate. 3. For adult patients with chronic severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy and when other systemic therapies are less appropriate, these medications are indicated. They should only be administered to patients who will be closely monitored and have regular follow-up visits with a physician. The recommended dose is 5 mg/kg intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 8 weeks. 4. These medications are indicated for reducing signs and symptoms in patients with active ankylosing spondylitis. The recommended dose is 5 mg/kg intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 6 weeks. 5. Infliximab is not to exceed 5 mg/kg per dose in patients with moderate-to-severe heart failure (NYHA class III or IV) due to contraindications. Patients should be evaluated for active tuberculosis and tested for latent infection prior to initiating treatment and periodically during therapy. 6. There is a higher incidence of serious infections in infliximab-treated patients aged 65 years or older; caution is advised in this population. 7. In pediatric patients aged 6 years and older with moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease who have had an inadequate response to conventional therapy, infliximab is indicated for reducing signs and symptoms and inducing and maintaining clinical remission. The recommended dose is 5 mg/kg intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 8 weeks. It has not been studied in children under 6 years of age. 8. Infliximab is also indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in children aged 6 years and older who have had an inadequate response to conventional therapy. The recommended dose is 5 mg/kg intravenously at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by every 8 weeks. Children should be up to date with immunizations before starting infliximab, and live vaccines should not be administered during treatment. 9. Infliximab and upadacitinib increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Infliximab and abatacept exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of serious infections. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Infliximab and adalimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Infliximab and alefacept both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Infliximab and anakinra both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Infliximab decreases the effects of the anthrax vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Immunosuppressants, including infliximab, increase the risk of infection when used with concomitant live vaccines. 16. Infliximab and antithymocyte globulin (equine or rabbit) both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Infliximab and axicabtagene ciloleucel both increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Infliximab and azathioprine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Infliximab and baricitinib increase each other’s toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Baricitinib is not recommended in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs, or potent immunosuppressives. 20. Infliximab and basiliximab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Infliximab decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Infliximab and brexucabtagene autoleucel both increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Infliximab and cyclosporine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Infliximab decreases the effects of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids (and acellular pertussis vaccine) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Infliximab and etanercept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Infliximab and everolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Infliximab and golimumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Infliximab decreases the effects of hepatitis A, hepatitis B, and hepatitis A/typhoid vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 33. Infliximab decreases the effects of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Infliximab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Infliximab and idecabtagene vicleucel both increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Infliximab decreases the effects of influenza virus vaccines (quadrivalent, trivalent, adjuvanted, cell-cultured, or intranasal) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 37. Infliximab decreases the effects of Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Infliximab and leflunomide both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Infliximab and lisocabtagene maraleucel both increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Infliximab decreases the effects of measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccines (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 41. Infliximab decreases the effects of meningococcal polysaccharide vaccine (ACYW-135) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 42. Infliximab and muromonab-CD3 both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Infliximab and mycophenolate both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 44. Infliximab and pexidartinib both increase toxicity risks. Pexidartinib is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents. 45. Infliximab decreases the effects of pneumococcal vaccines (13-valent and polyvalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 46. Infliximab and pretomanid both increase toxicity risks. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during treatment. 47. Infliximab decreases the effects of rabies vaccines (chick embryo cell-derived) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Infliximab and rilonacept both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 49. Infliximab decreases the effects of rotavirus oral vaccine (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Infliximab and selinexor both increase toxicity risks. Selinexor may cause neurological toxicities. Avoid coadministration with medications that cause dizziness or confusion. 51. Infliximab and sirolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 52. Infliximab decreases the effects of smallpox and mpox (vaccinia) vaccine (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Infliximab and tacrolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 54. Infliximab and temsirolimus both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 55. Infliximab decreases the effects of tetanus toxoid (adsorbed or fluid) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 56. Infliximab decreases the effects of tick-borne encephalitis vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Infliximab and tisagenlecleucel both increase each other’s immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 58. Infliximab and tocilizumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 59. Infliximab and tofacitinib both increase toxicity risks through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 60. Infliximab and tongkat ali both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 61. Infliximab decreases the effects of travelers’ diarrhea and cholera vaccines (inactivated) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 62. Infliximab decreases the effects of typhoid vaccines (polysaccharide and live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated.
